claim: For uniformly random \(X\in\{0,1\}^n\) with \(n\ge 2\), let \(\mathcal D_2(X)\) be the set of distinct length-\(n-2\) subsequences obtainable by exactly two deletions, and let \(B_n=|\mathcal D_2(X)|\). Then \(\operatorname{Var}(B_n)=\frac{(n-1)(n-2)(2n-3)}{32}\). Consequently \(\operatorname{sd}(B_n)=\frac14 n^{3/2}(1+O(n^{-1}))\).
integrity: The all-parameter proof is symbolic: it combines the exact run-length enumeration with an independent Bernoulli boundary representation and Walsh orthogonality. Exhaustive enumeration through length 12 is corroborative only.
scientific_limitations: The theorem is restricted to uniform binary centers and exactly two deletions; it does not determine higher moments, the full distribution, nonbinary analogues, or deletion-ball intersections.
title: Exact variance of binary two-deletion sphere size
